title: How do you create brainstorming buckets quickly when your mind goes blank?
description: Simple splits for brainstorming for case interviews. When you need buckets fast for "What else could they do?" A checklist, a worked example and how to say it
hook: When an interviewer asks for ideas and your mind goes blank, a simple split can rescue you. These pairs give you instant buckets for almost any brainstorm.
body:
When it helps

When you need buckets fast for "What else could they do?"

The splits

  • Internal vs external
  • Short term vs long term
  • Revenue vs costs
  • Supply vs demand
  • Quantitative vs qualitative
  • Pros vs cons
  • Organic vs inorganic
  • Direct vs indirect
  • Financial vs non-financial

An example

"How could a museum increase visitor numbers?" Pick a split: internal versus external. Internal: new exhibitions, longer opening hours, a better café, easier online booking. External: partnerships with schools, tourism boards, hotels, events in the city. In ten seconds you have two clean buckets, and you look organised even though you had no time to prepare.

How it sounds in an interview

Let me split this into what the client can change itself, and what involves outside partners. On the internal side...
